forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Hillingdon pension fund surplus hits £330m as investment returns lift funding to 124%
news_drafts.lead: Hillingdon's pension fund has swung to a surplus of £330m, up from £210m a year earlier, after delivering investment returns of 21.5% over 15 months to June. The fund's assets now cover 124% of its liabilities, up from 118%, meaning it has more than enough money to pay pensions promised to staff. The improvement means the fund needs annual investment returns of only 4.5% to stay fully funded, down from 5.1%, with a probability of 88% of achieving that target. Over five years, the fund has returned 6.7% annually, exactly matching its long-term objective, though it has underperformed its own benchmark by about 1% a year across all periods. The stronger short-term performance and improved funding position suggest recent strategy changes are beginning to take effect.

news_drafts.headline: Hillingdon on track for three-quarters of savings target, but risks mount
news_drafts.lead: Hillingdon Council has delivered £13.1m of its £27.1m savings programme for 2026/27 by the fourth month of the year, with a further £7.9m on track to follow. Combined, 77 per cent of the planned cuts and efficiencies are either achieved or progressing as intended. However, the council has identified £3.9m at risk of not delivering, including significant uncertainty around social housing supply schemes, and has marked £599,000 as unable to be delivered without alternative support. The Cabinet meeting on 17 September also heard that homelessness demand is rising against expectation—placements increased by 11 year-to-date against a budgeted reduction of 7—and that schools are facing a £13.1m overspend on high needs support for children with special educational needs as parents rush to apply before government reforms take effect.

news_drafts.headline: Hillingdon faces adverse homelessness trend despite lower opening numbers
news_drafts.lead: Hillingdon Council faces an adverse trend in homelessness demand despite opening the financial year with 155 fewer households in nightly-paid accommodation than budgeted. In the first four months, placements have increased by 11 against a budgeted reduction of 7, prompting the council to identify a £1.2m risk for the rest of the year. The council also faces a £13.1m overspend on schools funding for children with special needs, driven by parents applying before government reforms take effect; under a temporary government rule, this overspend is recorded outside the council's main accounts. The council has nonetheless delivered or is tracking to achieve three-quarters of its £27.1m annual savings programme. Its capital programme shows a £31.7m underspend—a quarter of budgeted capital spending—which the council plans to carry forward to later years.

findings.paper_title: 6 Investment Strategy and Fund Manager Performance Update Part 1
findings.headline: Fund underperformed its own benchmark by 0.9-1.1% p.a. across all measured periods, though meeting long-term actuarial targets and improving.
findings.detail: The Fund has consistently underperformed its benchmark across all reported time periods by approximately 0.9% to 1.1% per annum, though it has met its long-term actuarial discount rate of 6.7% over five years. The paper notes shorter-term performance has started to improve following strategy changes over recent years. While outperforming the LGPS average over 1, 3 and 5-year periods, the fund ranked in the lower half of peers over longer periods (92nd and 97th over 10 and 20 years respectively).
findings.matters: Consistent underperformance against the fund's own targets indicates investment strategy may need refinement; a finance director would want to understand whether recent improvements are sustainable.
findings.figures: Benchmark underperformance 0.9-1.1% p.a.; fund returned 11.7%, 9.1%, 5.9% p.a. vs benchmarks of 12.7%, 10.0%, 7.0% over 1, 3, 5 years; longer-term peer rankings 92nd (10yr), 97th (20yr)
findings.quote: the Fund has underperformed its own benchmark across all reported periods, by approximately 0.9% to 1.1% per annum

findings.paper_title: 6 Investment Strategy and Fund Manager Performance Update Part 1
findings.headline: Pension fund funding level improved from 114% to 124% in one quarter, with surplus rising by £140m.
findings.detail: The Fund's estimated funding level increased from 114% to 124% and the funding surplus rose from £0.19bn to £0.33bn in the quarter to 30 June 2026. The improvement was driven primarily by strong investment performance, with fund assets increasing by approximately £130m. The required annual return to achieve full funding fell from 5.1% to 4.5%, while the probability of achieving it improved from 84% to 88%.
findings.matters: A significantly better-funded pension scheme reduces the risk of future calls on the council's finances and improves overall financial resilience.
findings.figures: Funding level 114% to 124% (+10 percentage points); surplus £0.19bn to £0.33bn (+£0.14bn); assets increased £130m; required return fell from 5.1% to 4.5% p.a.; probability of success improved from 84% to 88%
findings.quote: the Fund's estimated funding level increasing from 114% to 124% and the funding surplus rising from £0.19bn to £0.33bn, an improvement of approximately £140m

findings.paper_title: 6b. Hymans Interim Funding update at 30 Jun 2026
findings.headline: Probability of meeting pension fund investment targets increased to 88% from 86%.
findings.detail: The likelihood that the fund's investment strategy will achieve its required 4.5% annual return improved by 2 percentage points. Combined with the lower required return threshold, this indicates better probability of the fund maintaining its improved funding position.
findings.matters: Higher success probability reduces the risk of unexpected shortfalls requiring additional council contributions to the pension fund.
findings.quote: Return likelihood 88% +2% vs last valuation Required return (% pa)* 4.5% -0.6% vs last valuation

findings.paper_title: 6b. Hymans Interim Funding update at 30 Jun 2026
findings.headline: Fund achieved 21.51% investment returns over 15 months to June 2026.
findings.detail: Strong investment performance from 1 April 2025 to 30 June 2026 drove the improvement in the funding position. This substantial return reduced the required annual investment return to reach full funding from 5.1% to 4.5% pa.
findings.matters: Strong investment returns reduce the funding gap and lower the hurdle rate the council's pension scheme needs to clear, improving long-term financial sustainability.
findings.figures: Total investment return 21.51%, required return fell from 5.1% to 4.5% pa

findings.paper_title: 6b. Hymans Interim Funding update at 30 Jun 2026
findings.headline: Pension fund surplus increased by £120m to £330m with funding level improving to 124%.
findings.detail: The fund's surplus grew from £210m at 31 March 2025 to £330m at 30 June 2026. The funding level (assets expressed as a percentage of liabilities) improved from 118% to 124%, with assets reaching £1.71bn against total liabilities of £1.38bn.
findings.matters: A growing and increasingly overfunded pension scheme reduces the likelihood of future cash calls on the council's budget and improves the council's financial stability.
findings.quote: Surplus/(deficit) £0.33bn +£0.12bn vs last valuation Funding level 124% +6% vs last valuation
